extracted.intended_audience: prospective applicants to the Wallace Stegner Fellowship (writers applying to Stanford's two-year fiction or poetry fellowship)
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and applying for Stanford's Wallace Stegner two-year creative-writing fellowship (5 fiction and 5 poetry fellowships per year). The page describes eligibility, selection principles, responsibilities, timelines, and financial/ residency expectations for fellows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of the candidate’s creative work
rubrics_metrics.description: In awarding fellowships, we consider the quality of the candidate’s creative work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program looks for talent and seriousness; fellows are diverse in style and experience, and the quality of submitted creative work is a primary factor in selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential for growth
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection considers the candidate's potential for growth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The fellowship is aimed at promising writers to spend two years developing their writing; applicants who show capacity to develop further are favored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to contribute to and profit from workshops
rubrics_metrics.description: We consider an applicant’s ability to contribute to and profit from our writing workshops.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should demonstrate they will both benefit from faculty-led critique and actively add value to peer workshops; selection favors those likely to engage productively in the cohort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to writing and workshop attendance (only requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: The only requirements are writing and workshop attendance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fellows are expected to write, revise, and continue writing; attend a 3-hour weekly faculty-led workshop that coincides with Stanford's academic calendar; this commitment is the fundamental obligation of fellows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrated practice of revision toward a finished manuscript
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellows are required to write, revise, and then write again, with the goal of a finished manuscript ready for publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program expects sustained production and revision aimed at creating publishable manuscripts over the two-year period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active engagement with cohort's work (reading and commenting)
rubrics_metrics.description: As part of the workshop, fellows are expected to actively engage with their cohort's work by reading and thoughtfully commenting on pieces presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Workshop participation includes substantive, thoughtful critique of peers' work; being a constructive workshop participant is an explicit expectation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Residency / proximity requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A fellow must live close enough to Stanford in order to attend workshops, readings, and events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Residency near campus is required because weekly, in-person 3-hour workshops and program events are mandatory; remote participation is not presented as an option.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full-time fellowship commitment (no concurrent degree or full-time job)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Stegner Fellowship is a full-time academic commitment and is not intended to be pursued concurrently with another degree program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The purpose is to give writers as much time as possible for writing; holding a full-time job or pursuing another degree runs counter to the program's intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Age requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must be at least 18 years old when they start the fellowship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historically accepted fellows have ranged in age from 22 to 75; the only hard floor is 18.

rubrics_metrics.name: No degrees or tests required; open to all nationalities
rubrics_metrics.description: We do not require any degrees or tests for admission. Anyone may apply, regardless of nationality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If accepted, non-U.S. citizens are considered non-matriculated graduate students for visa purposes and the program will assist with obtaining a J-1 visa.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior publication is not required (and may indicate reduced fit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior book publication is not required; note that prior publication may suggest a career that has advanced beyond the point when the fellowship’s instruction and workshop critique are most useful in a writer's development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants with extensive publication histories may be less well-matched to the fellowship's developmental aims; lack of publication is not a barrier.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection values: diversity of style/experience, talent and seriousness
rubrics_metrics.description: Our fellows are diverse in style and experience, with talent and seriousness the true common denominators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program explicitly does not favor a particular 'school of writing' and values a range of backgrounds and approaches while emphasizing seriousness about craft.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program structure and fellow obligations (duration, workshop length, summer off)
rubrics_metrics.description: 2-year fellowship; fellows convene weekly in a 3-hour workshop with faculty; workshop coincides with Stanford's academic calendar and fellows have the summer off.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are staggered admissions so 10 first-year and 10 second-year fellows are present each year; fellows should expect intensive academic-year workshop involvement and summer independent work or travel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial and administrative expectations (stipend, tuition, health insurance)
rubrics_metrics.description: The fellowship includes a $75,000 living stipend per academic year; the program pays each fellow’s tuition and health insurance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Bay Area is expensive; some fellows may need to supplement income depending on individual needs (often via summer work); teaching appointments to supplement income are not guaranteed and priority may go to Ph.D. students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participation in program events (readings, lecture series, visiting writers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellows are encouraged to attend reading events and lecture series hosted by the program; during the first year fellows participate in the Stegner Fellow Reading series where they give a public reading of their work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attendance at public readings, colloquiums, and visiting-writer events enriches the fellowship experience; fellows should plan to participate in public-facing program activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application timeline and notification
rubrics_metrics.description: Application window: opens on September 1 and closes on November 3 at 11:59 pm PST; all applicants are notified of fellowship decisions in April.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should submit within the stated window and expect decisions in April; the next application round opens Sept 1.
